Apple is about to announce its Q3 FY2026 earnings, followed by what will be Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO. Here's how to listen in live.

Ongoing component shortages are expected to continue playing a significant role.

Half an hour after market close, Apple will announce its Q3 FY2026 earnings, followed by a conference call with CEO Tim Cook and CFO Kevan Parekh. This will be Tim Cook's final earnings call as Apple's CEO, and the 90th of his tenure.

On last quarter's call, incoming CEO John Ternus made a brief appearance, thanking Cook, Apple's management team, employees, and long-term shareholders for their support, while expressing optimism about the company's future.

Last quarter, Apple guided for year-over-year revenue growth between 14% and 17%, with gross margins between 47.5% and 48.5%. That implied revenue of roughly $107.2 billion to $110 billion, against a Wall Street consensus of approximately $109 billion.

Apple is expected to address the ongoing impact of component shortages, its recent price increases, and its outlook for future demand on the earnings call.

Apple's call will begin at 2:00 PM Pacific / 5:00 PM Eastern, with management delivering prepared remarks before moving to the analyst Q&A segment.

As always, the call will be live-streamed and you can listen in via the link below.

Stay tuned to 9to5Mac later today for full coverage of Apple's Q3 2026 earnings, including highlights from the call.
